pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 16-week study in patients ≥12 years with eosinophilic asthma (blood eosinophils ≥400/µL) inadequately controlled on ICS
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in FEV1 over 16 weeks
pivotal_trials.result: Treatment difference (reslizumab 3 mg/kg vs placebo): +0.160 L (95% CI 0.060, 0.259); p=0.0018

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 52-week study in patients ≥12 years with eosinophilic asthma (blood eosinophils ≥400/µL)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency of asthma exacerbations per patient during 52-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted exacerbation rate: reslizumab 0.90/year vs placebo 1.80/year; Rate Ratio 0.50 (95% CI 0.37, 0.67); p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 52-week study in patients ≥12 years with eosinophilic asthma (blood eosinophils ≥400/µL)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Frequency of asthma exacerbations per patient during 52-week treatment period
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted exacerbation rate: reslizumab 0.86/year vs placebo 2.11/year; Rate Ratio 0.41 (95% CI 0.28, 0.59); p<0.0001

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 16-week study in patients 18–65 years with moderate-to-severe asthma unselected for baseline blood eosinophil levels (4:1 reslizumab:placebo)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Interaction between baseline blood eosinophil count and change in FEV1 at Week 16
pivotal_trials.result: Primary interaction not significant (slope difference 0.31, p=0.23); however, in the ≥400 cells/µL subgroup (n=96), treatment difference in FEV1 at Week 16 was +0.270 L (95% CI 0.008, 0.532; p=0.0436)

advisory_committee.vote: 11-3 favorable for adult approval; 0-14 against adolescent approval

boxed_warning.full_text:
WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS

Anaphylaxis has been observed with CINQAIR infusion in 0.3% of patients in placebo-controlled clinical studies. Anaphylaxis was reported as early as the second dose of CINQAIR.

Anaphylaxis can be life-threatening. Patients should be observed for an appropriate period of time after CINQAIR administration by a healthcare professional prepared to manage anaphylaxis. Discontinue CINQAIR immediately if the patient experiences signs or symptoms of anaphylaxis.

key_safety: Reslizumab was associated with anaphylaxis (4 cases in ~1028 treated patients, vs 0 placebo), CPK elevations (moderate/severe/life-threatening in 18% reslizumab vs 14% placebo), higher malignancy incidence (0.6% vs 0.3%), and increased pneumonia in patients on baseline oral corticosteroids (7% vs 1%).
target_moa: Humanized anti-interleukin-5 (IL-5) monoclonal antibody; binds IL-5 and blocks its interaction with the IL-5 receptor, reducing eosinophil differentiation, maturation, recruitment, and activation

_meta.indication:
CINQAIR is indicated for the add-on maintenance treatment of patients with severe asthma aged 18 years and older with an eosinophilic phenotype.
Limitation of Use:
- CINQAIR is not indicated for treatment of other eosinophilic conditions.
- CINQAIR is not indicated for the relief of acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus.

indication_details.population_restrictions: aged 18 years and older; eosinophilic phenotype; severe asthma
indication_details.combination: in combination with existing maintenance therapy ('add-on maintenance treatment')

advisory_committee_detail.vote: Adults (18+): Efficacy 13 Yes / 1 No / 0 Abstain; Safety 11 Yes / 3 No / 0 Abstain; Approval 11 Yes / 3 No / 0 Abstain. Pediatrics (12-17): Efficacy 0 Yes / 14 No / 0 Abstain; Approval 0 Yes / 14 No / 0 Abstain.
advisory_committee_detail.discussion_summary: The PADAC reviewed reslizumab's efficacy and safety for severe eosinophilic asthma, discussing the target population, dose-ranging adequacy, adolescent data, ethnic subgroup data, anaphylaxis findings (including the role of alpha-gal), and muscle enzyme elevations. The committee voted to support approval in adults 18 and older, finding the eosinophilic phenotype and exacerbation history a supportable narrow indication, while unanimously voting against approval in patients 12-17 years due to a paradoxical increase in exacerbation rates and limited data. Members felt anaphylaxis risk was manageable through labeling given the IV administration in healthcare settings.

linkages.concern: Anaphylaxis was a major safety finding; committee members thought it 'could be managed through labeling, particularly given that the product will be administered in health care facility because of IV dosing'
linkages.change: A boxed warning for anaphylaxis was added to the prescribing information

linkages.concern: Limited and paradoxical efficacy data in patients 12 to 17 years of age (point estimate favoring placebo for exacerbations) led the committee to unanimously vote against approval in adolescents
linkages.change: Indicated age restricted to 18 years and older; pediatric 12-17 age group excluded from approval; waiver granted for IV formulation studies in children under 12

linkages.concern: Committee members were supportive of the 'narrow target population identified by previous history of asthma exacerbation, and of the eosinophil phenotype'; role of blood eosinophil counts in determining target population was a key discussion issue
linkages.change: Indication restricted to 'severe asthma with an eosinophilic phenotype'; blood eosinophil count threshold (≥400 cells/µL at baseline) referenced in the Clinical Trials labeling section

linkages.concern: Lack of dose-ranging data was noted by committee members, though they 'were not overly concerned because of demonstration of efficacy and lack of definite dose related safety findings'
linkages.change: Teva's proposed dose of 3 mg/kg IV every 4 weeks was accepted as-is; no additional dose-ranging studies required prior to approval
